title: Who are the top consulting firms, and how are they usually grouped?
description: A map of the consulting world: MBB, the Big Four and their strategy arms, Accenture, other strategy firms, specialists and boutiques.
hook: The top consulting firms are usually grouped into MBB (McKinsey, BCG and Bain), the Big Four (Deloitte, PwC, EY and KPMG) and their strategy arms, Accenture, a set of other well-known strategy firms such as Oliver Wyman, Kearney and Roland Berger, and specialist boutiques. Each group does a different mix of work and interviews in a slightly different way. Here is the whole map in one place, with a method for turning it into your own target list.

The map at a glance

GroupFirmsMain kind of work
MBBMcKinsey, BCG, BainStrategy for senior leaders, plus operations and implementation
Big FourDeloitte, PwC, EY, KPMGBroad: technology, operations, risk, deals, people, with dedicated strategy arms
AccentureAccentureTechnology and operations at very large scale, with a strategy business
Other strategy firmsOliver Wyman, Kearney, Roland Berger, L.E.K., OC&C, Simon-Kucher and othersStrategy, often strong in particular industries, functions or regions
Boutiques and in-houseHundreds of firms; corporate strategy teamsOne industry, function or region; or strategy inside one company

The labels are shorthand, not a ranking of quality. They tell you roughly what work a firm does and how hard its interviews tend to be.

MBB: McKinsey, BCG and Bain

The three best-known strategy firms, sometimes called the Big Three. They focus on senior-level problems such as strategy, M&A, growth and large transformations, and all three also do substantial operations and implementation work. They recruit from universities, business schools and experienced professionals, and their interviews are among the most competitive.

They interview in similar ways, with case interviews and personal experience questions at the centre, but the style differs: McKinsey's cases are usually interviewer-led, while BCG and Bain usually expect you to drive. How McKinsey, BCG and Bain differ covers this in detail.

The Big Four and their strategy arms

Deloitte, PwC, EY and KPMG began as accounting and audit firms and now also sell tax, advisory and consulting services. They are far larger than MBB. For fiscal 2025, the last year for which all four had reported as of November 2026, their global revenues were:

FirmFiscal 2025 revenueYear ended
Deloitte$70.5BMay 2025
PwC$56.9BJune 2025
EY$53.2BJune 2025
KPMG$39.8BSeptember 2025

That is about $220B combined, with roughly 1.5 million people between them. Deloitte has since reported $74.5B for fiscal 2026. These totals cover audit and tax as well as consulting, so they show scale, not the size of each consulting business.

Big Four consulting is broad, with large technology, operations, risk and implementation practices. Each firm also has a strategy arm whose work is closest to MBB:

  • Deloitte: Monitor Deloitte, built on Monitor Group, which Deloitte acquired in 2013.
  • PwC: Strategy&, the former Booz & Company, which PwC acquired in 2014.
  • EY: EY-Parthenon, built on The Parthenon Group, acquired in 2014. In 2025 EY folded its wider Strategy and Transactions business into EY-Parthenon, taking it past 25,000 people.
  • KPMG: its strategy group.

More on the Big Four, including how their consulting differs from MBB.

Accenture

A global professional services company best known for technology, outsourcing and operations work, with a strategy consulting business too. It is often compared with the Big Four because of its size and its technology focus, although it has no audit business. Accenture Strategy's interview process is covered separately.

Other strategy firms

A group of well-regarded strategy firms sits between MBB and the rest. Examples include Oliver Wyman (part of Marsh McLennan, with deep financial services work), Kearney, Roland Berger (founded in Germany and strong in Europe), L.E.K. Consulting, OC&C and Simon-Kucher (known for pricing). They are sometimes called tier two, but that label undersells them: many candidates choose them for their culture, their industry depth or the earlier responsibility a smaller team can offer. Their interviews are case-based and often just as demanding. What these firms are like to interview with, and Oliver Wyman's process in particular.

Specialists, boutiques and in-house teams

Boutiques focus on one industry (healthcare, energy, retail), one function (pricing, people, supply chain) or one region. They can offer deep expertise and early client contact, and are worth a serious look if you already know the field you love.

In-house strategy teams sit inside large companies, often staffed by former consultants. They work on one company's problems over a longer horizon and typically hire through case-style interviews too, so the same preparation applies.

Building your target list

Do not apply only to the names you know. Start with three questions, then build a list across several groups.

  1. What kind of problem do you want? Strategy, operations, technology, deals or a particular industry.
  2. Where do you want to live? Firms differ greatly by city, and smaller offices hire fewer people.
  3. Which team? The practice or group you join shapes your work more than the brand on the door.

An example

Take a candidate who wants to work in London, enjoys healthcare and wants strategy work with some implementation. A sensible list might be:

  • MBB: all three, since the preparation overlaps heavily.
  • Big Four strategy arms: Monitor Deloitte, Strategy& and EY-Parthenon, plus the healthcare consulting team at one Big Four firm.
  • Other strategy firms: L.E.K. and Oliver Wyman, both with life sciences and healthcare work, and one more generalist such as Kearney.
  • One specialist: a healthcare boutique.

That is around ten firms across four groups. For each, note one recent project or practice area you could discuss, the interview format your recruiter confirms, the deadline, and one reason your experience fits. That last line becomes your answer to "Why this firm?"

Applying across groups also means more real interviews, and more interviews make you better at interviewing. Order your applications so the earlier ones give you practice before the firms you care about most, where deadlines allow.

Common mistakes

  • Treating labels as rankings. "Tier two" says little about the quality of a specific team or the career it leads to.
  • Ignoring the team. A Big Four strategy arm and its technology practice can be very different jobs. Read the role description, not just the firm name.
  • Applying too narrowly. Three MBB applications and nothing else leaves you with no practice and no fallback.
  • Applying too broadly. Thirty generic applications read as generic. Each firm on your list should have a real reason behind it.
  • Relying on old information. Practice names, structures and processes change. Check each firm's own careers pages and confirm the format with your recruiter.

Practice

1. A friend says, "I only want strategy work, so I'll only apply to MBB." What would you suggest?

Show the answer

Strategy work also happens at the Big Four strategy arms (Monitor Deloitte, Strategy&, EY-Parthenon), at firms like Oliver Wyman, Kearney, Roland Berger and L.E.K., and in in-house strategy teams. Adding several of these widens the chances of an offer without changing the kind of work, and gives your friend real interview practice before the MBB rounds.

2. Using the fiscal 2025 figures, roughly what share of the Big Four's combined revenue did Deloitte earn?

Show the answer

$70.5B ÷ $220.4B ≈ 32%, or nearly a third. A quick way to check: a quarter of $220B is $55B, and Deloitte is well above that.

3. You want to live in Manchester and work on energy projects. How would you start your list?

Show the answer

Check which firms have a Manchester office or hire into it, then look for energy and utilities practices at each: the Big Four and Accenture are likely to have the most regional presence, and a specialist energy consultancy may be worth adding. Then add a few London-based strategy firms with strong energy work in case you are willing to relocate or travel. Confirm the roles and formats on each firm's careers pages.

Where to go next

Read the types of consulting to decide which work you want, then how consulting recruiting works to plan your timeline. Once your list is set, start building the core skills with the case interview guide.
